newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Feb 4.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Feb 4.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a move that may see the two companies that dominate stevedoring in Australia - P&O Ports and Patrick Stevedoring - facing a major new competitor, Hong Kong-based shipping giant Orient Overseas Container Line yesterday became preferred bidder to devlop a new cargo terminal in the Port of Melbourne. Page 1.

According to documents tendered in Sydney's St James Local Court yesterday, Simon Hannes, a high-flying executive director of Macquarie Bank who is regarded as one of Australia's leading corporate advisers, used the name "Mark Booth" or "M. Booth" in coducting a series of non-reportable cash transactions. Page 1.

George Palmer, QC, acting for the new trustees of the failed trusts seeking to recover some of the A$640 million placed by 52,000 unit holders, told the Victorian Supreme Court yesterday Burns Philp Trustee Co was a "sleeping sentry" while investors' funds were drained from the Estate Mortgage Trusts into hazardous speculative projects. Page 3.

BHP Petroleum is believed to have struck a deal, completed in principle and awaiting ratification by the Vietnam Government before being approved by the BHP board, with its partner, the Malaysian Government-owned oil company Petronas, to sell the disastrous Dai Hung oil project. Page 17.

Results from Shell Australia operated well Cornea 2, in Western Australia's offshore Browse Basin in the North West Shelf area - now recognised as one of the world's hottest exploration sites - has sparked a run on oil stocks holding offshore Western Austalian territory when locally listed Cultus Petroleum revealed a discovery with the potential to contain more than 100 million barrels of oil. Page 17.

Ron Paul, the chairman of Queensland-based engineering and electrical group Evans Deakin Industries Ltd, said yesterday the group had returned a 50 percent increase in net profit to A$9.08 million for the half year and is on track to post another record annual result following the A$200 million purchase of Clyde Industries Ltd. Page 17.
THE AUSTRALIAN

According to documents tendered by the St James Local Court in Sydney yesterday, high-profile Macquarie Bank Ltd executive Simon Hannes, who was arrested by the Australian Federal Police on January 20 and charged on one count under the Financial Transactions Reports Act, is linked to the mysterious trader "Mark Booth", who made a A$1.98 million profit trading TNT Ltd options prior to the takeover of the company. Page 17.

In a move which confirms its strategic shift towards wider representation in the Asia-Pacific region, National Australia Bank has announced its third Asian banking licence in recent months - an offshore banking licence in Malaysia. It is the first time Malaysia has granted such a licence to an Australian bank and it gives NAB an edge in offshore banking. Page 17.

According to report by the PA Consulting Group, foreign firms are set to beat local businesses in the rush for lucrative government contracts as the public sector embraces the push to outsourcing. The report found the local market is too small to cope with the expected boom in government demand for private contractors. Page 17.

As Optus Communications prepares to spend A$25 million to upgrade its Aurora satellite to digital transmission, Optus Vision has revealed it is planning to deliver its pay-TV service by satellite as well as cable, naming Bill Blamires, formerly Australis Media corporate treasurer, as chief executive for its joint satellite venture with Australis. Page 19.

In a move which sets it on course for another record year profit, engineering group Evans Deakin Industries has posted a 50 percent increase in December-half earnings to A$9 million, including an abnormal profit of A$481,000 on the sale of Clyde's equity in Sunbeam Victa. Page 19.

The Ten Group has poached David White, the chief executive of Telecasters Australia - Ten's affiliate station in northern New South Wales and regional Queensland - to fill the role of general manager of news and current affairs. White announced his resignaion yesterday from the top executive job at Telecasters. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Commonwealth Director of Public Prosecutions tendered allegations yesterday that Macquarie Bank executive director Simon Gautier Hannes visited 15 different bank branches in one day to collect nine bank cheques, each worth less than A$10,000. The cheques were made in favour of Perpetual Trustee Co Ltd-Ord Minnett Cash Management Trust. Hannes is charged with breaching laws governing large cash transactions, and will plead not guilty. Page 25.

Unit holders in the collapsed Estate Mortgage trusts are claiming damages totalling A$677 million for negligence from former trustees Burns Philp Trustee Company and a number of third parties. Trustees acting for 45,000 unit holders allege high-risk investment practices from the former trustees, and say the image of Estate Mortgage trusts as being safe and cautious was an illusion. Page 25.

BHP is yet to confirm the sale of its controlling interest in the loss-making Dai Hung offshore oilfield in Vietnam. BHP recorded a A$55 million operating loss on the project for 1995/96 as the oilfield failed to live up to its expectations. BHP's controlling 43.7 percent stake was written down to a zero carrying value after the loss, and Malaysia's state-owned oil company, Petronas, is expected to buy the shares. Page 25.

Bureau of Statistics figures on building approvals released yesterday show New South Wales continuing to outperform the rest of the nation. In New South Wales, total approvals rose 2.7 percent in December compared to a one percent nationwide fall. Private homes were up 7.5 percent in December with the surge being attributed to three interest rate cuts in the second half of 1996. Page 27.

Professor Peter Dodd has been appointed as the new head of the Australian Graduate School of Management. The school, part of the University of New South Wales, is regarded as among the top three management and business schools in the country. Professor Dodd, a former merchant banker, replaces Professor Fred Hilmer. Page 27.

A rare private criminal prosecution against five Commonwealth Bank officers may be terminated if the matter is handed to the Commonwealth Director of Public Prosecutions. Brewing engineer and plant builder Rodney Zemanek instigated the prosecution, alleging the officers forced him into receivership last year by freezing his loan accounts. Magistrate Geoff Cleary adjourned the case to allow the DPP to consider if there was sufficient evidence to prosecute the officers. Page 27.
THE AGE

In a move which will see the end of BHP Petroleum's failed involvement in the Dai Hung oil project off the southern coast of Vietnam, Malaysia's State-owned oil company Petronas said in Kuala Lumpur yesterday it had acquired BHPP's 43.75 percent stake in the project for an undisclosed sum. Page C1.

National Australia Bank has become the first Australian bank to win an offshore banking licence in Malaysia, in a move that takes NAB one step further than ANZ in the ongoing battle for domination in the Asian market. NAB group general manager Bob Prowse said the licence will allow the bank to offer services to its customers in Australasia, the United States, Britain and Ireland. Page C1.

According to a statement of facts handed up in Sydney's St James Court yesterday, top Macquarie Bank executive Mark Hannes, who was arrested in January and charged with breaching laws governing large cash transactions, used the name Mark Booth as an alias. Page C1.

A Coles Myer spokeswoman revealed yesterday the group is planning to introduce Electronic Funds Transfer at Point of Sale (EFTPOS) into department stores - close to a decade after it did so in its supermarkets. However, department store customers will only be able to use the system to make purchases, not cash withdrawals. Page C1.

Nine months after acquiring shares in property funds management group Heine Management, controversial Hong Kong-based Regent Pacific Corp has sold its 14.9 percent stake in the group and has left with profits of about A$850,000. The release of the stock into the markets yesterday allowed FAI Insurances to secure a 19.9 percent stake in Heine. Page C3.

Manly Local Court was told yesterday the Commonwealth Bank has approached the Commonwealth Director of Public Prosecutions to terminate a private criminal prosecution brought by Rodney Zemanek, a former borrower, against five of CBA's senior bank oficers. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
